title: Degree-domination criterion for a Hamiltonian path (Clapham Ex. 4.2.5(a))
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with complement $G^{c}$, and arrange the vertex degrees of each graph in nondecreasing order, writing $d_{0} \le d_{1} \le \cdots \le d_{n-1}$ for the sorted degree sequence of $G$ and $d'_{0} \le d'_{1} \le \cdots \le d'_{n-1}$ for that of $G^{c}$. If $d'_{m} \le d_{m}$ for every index $m$ with $2m \le n$, then $G$ has a Hamiltonian path: there are vertices $a$ and $b$ and a walk from $a$ to $b$ that visits every vertex of $G$ exactly once.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph on n vertices
degrees of G listed in nondecreasing order (σ sorts G-degrees)
degrees of the complement G^c listed in nondecreasing order (τ sorts G^c-degrees)

\textbf{4.2.5} (a) Let $G$ be a simple graph with degree sequence $(d_1, d_2, \ldots,
d_\nu)$ and let $G^c$ have degree sequence $(d_1', d_2', \ldots, d_\nu')$ where $d_1 \le
d_2 \le \ldots \le d_\nu$ and $d_1' \le d_2' \le \ldots \le d_\nu'$. Show that if $d_m
\ge d_m'$ for all $m \le \nu/2$, then $G$ has a Hamilton path.
